refined_question: Let G be a group and let H_1, H_2, …, H_k be subgroups of G each of finite index, with k>1. Choose elements g_1, g_2, …, g_k in G, and consider the left cosets g_i H_i for i=1,…,k. Suppose these cosets are pairwise disjoint and that their union is G. Must it then be the case that the indices [G : H_1], [G : H_2], …, [G : H_k] are not all distinct (i.e., at least two of these indices coincide)?
justification: The name “Herzog–Schönheim conjecture” indicates only that this is a conjecture by Herzog and Schönheim, without conveying any information about cosets, partitions, or index conditions—in other words, it captures almost none of the content (completeness score 2). To state the conjecture fully, one must specify the group-theoretic context (groups, subgroups, cosets), the finiteness and partition conditions, the requirement k>1, and the conclusion about indices. The refined question reproduces the canonical formulation exactly, in a self-contained way faithful to the original source. No alternate formulation is given in the source.
